---
title: "Missing Date Investigation"
subtitle: "Recovering Board Approval Dates for 16 World Bank Costa Rica Projects"
date: today
---

```{r setup}
#| include: false
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(readr)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(lubridate)
library(scales)
source(here("R", "functions.R"))

projects_all     <- read_csv(here("data", "processed", "projects_all.csv"),      show_col_types = FALSE)
enrichment       <- read_csv(here("data", "processed", "date_enrichment.csv"),   show_col_types = FALSE)
projects_enr     <- read_csv(here("data", "processed", "projects_enriched.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
annual_scen      <- read_csv(here("data", "derived",   "annual_scenarios.csv"),  show_col_types = FALSE)
new_additions    <- read_csv(here("data", "derived",   "recovered_projects.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
```

> **Objective:** 16 of 72 World Bank Costa Rica project records had missing `boardapprovaldate` values
> in the original V2 API pull. This report documents the investigation, the recovery method, 
> the results, and their implications for the timeline analysis.

---

## 1. Baseline: the 16 missing-date projects

```{r baseline-table}
#| echo: false
missing <- projects_all |>
  filter(is.na(approval_year)) |>
  mutate(
    fin_status = case_when(
      is.na(totalamt)  ~ "Missing",
      totalamt == 0    ~ "Zero",
      TRUE             ~ paste0("$", round(totalamt/1e6, 0), "M")
    )
  )

missing |>
  select(`Project ID` = id, `Project name` = project_name,
         `Commitment` = fin_status, `Status` = status,
         `Instrument` = lendinginstr, `Sector 1` = sector1_name,
         `Close date` = close_date) |>
  mutate(`Close date` = substr(as.character(`Close date`), 1, 10)) |>
  kable(caption = "The 16 projects with missing boardapprovaldate in the original V2 API response") |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), font_size = 12)
```

```{r crosstab}
#| echo: false
projects_all |>
  mutate(
    date_status = if_else(is.na(approval_year), "Missing date", "Has date"),
    fin_status  = case_when(
      is.na(totalamt)  ~ "Missing amount",
      totalamt == 0    ~ "Zero",
      TRUE             ~ "Positive"
    )
  ) |>
  count(date_status, fin_status) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = fin_status, values_from = n, values_fill = 0L) |>
  rename(`Date availability` = date_status) |>
  kable(caption = "Cross-tabulation: approval date availability × financing status") |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"))
```

**Financing at stake in missing-date projects:**

```{r fin-summary}
#| echo: false
missing_fin <- missing |> filter(fin_status != "Zero")
total_pos_all  <- sum(projects_all$totalamt[!is.na(projects_all$totalamt) & projects_all$totalamt > 0])
total_pos_miss <- sum(missing$totalamt[!is.na(missing$totalamt) & missing$totalamt > 0])

tribble(
  ~Metric, ~Value,
  "Missing-date projects with positive commitment", as.character(sum(!is.na(missing$totalamt) & missing$totalamt > 0)),
  "Missing-date projects with zero commitment", as.character(sum(!is.na(missing$totalamt) & missing$totalamt == 0)),
  "Total positive financing in undated projects (nominal USD)", fmt_millions(total_pos_miss),
  "Total positive financing in all 72 projects (nominal USD)", fmt_billions(total_pos_all),
  "Undated projects' share of total positive financing", paste0(round(100 * total_pos_miss / total_pos_all, 1), "%")
) |>
  kable() |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"))
```

---

## 2. Date recovery method

### What was tried

The original data used the **World Bank Projects Search API V2** (`search.worldbank.org/api/v2/projects`), 
which returns `boardapprovaldate` as null for these 16 projects.

Three additional sources were checked in sequence:

1. **WB Project Detail Pages** (`projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/project-detail/{id}`) — 
   These are JavaScript single-page applications (SPAs). The raw HTML does not contain the project data; 
   it is loaded by Angular components from the API. Not suitable for scraping.

2. **WB Document API** (`search.worldbank.org/api/v2/wds`) — Returns document metadata with 
   document disclosure dates (`docdt`), not board approval dates. Used to estimate approximate 
   preparation periods but not to recover specific dates.

3. **WB Projects API V3** (`search.worldbank.org/api/v3/projects`) and **WB Bulk Excel Download** 
   (`search.worldbank.org/api/v3/projects/all.xlsx`, downloaded 2026-10-30) — **Both V3 and Excel 
   contained `boardapprovaldate` for 15 of the 16 projects.** V3 API and Excel agreed on all 15 dates 
   with zero discrepancies.

### Source reliability

- **V3 API and bulk Excel (2026-10-30)** are two delivery channels of the same World Bank database.
- Agreement across both independent output channels for all 15 recovered dates gives **high confidence** 
  that these are the WB's authoritative board approval dates for those projects.
- Three dates fall on **June 30** (fiscal year end): P006930, P006950, P006951. These are a common WB 
  convention for projects without a precise approval date recorded in the system. The year is likely 
  correct; the June 30 date is a fiscal year approximation.
- **P169724** (Learning for All, $100M, Dropped) has no date in either V3 or Excel. This is the only 
  genuinely unresolvable case.

---

## 3. Recovery results

```{r recovery-table}
#| echo: false
enrichment |>
  mutate(
    recovered_date_display = if_else(
      !is.na(recovered_date),
      format(as.Date(recovered_date), "%Y-%m-%d"),
      "—"
    ),
    totalamt_display = case_when(
      is.na(totalamt) | totalamt == 0 ~ "$0",
      TRUE ~ fmt_millions(totalamt)
    ),
    conf_short = case_when(
      grepl("High", confidence)   ~ "High",
      grepl("Medium", confidence) ~ "Med (FY proxy)",
      TRUE                        ~ "Not recovered"
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(recovered_year) |>
  select(
    `Project ID`    = id,
    `Project name`  = project_name,
    `Recovered date` = recovered_date_display,
    `Year`          = recovered_year,
    `Confidence`    = conf_short,
    `Commitment`    = totalamt_display,
    `Status`        = status,
    Notes           = notes
  ) |>
  kable(caption = "Recovered board approval dates for 16 missing-date projects (Sources: WB V3 API and bulk Excel, cross-validated)") |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), font_size = 11)
```

```{r recovery-fig}
#| fig-cap: "The 16 missing-date projects placed on a timeline. Point size proportional to commitment amount. Projects outside the 1990–2024 window are greyed out or shown in amber."
knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "fig10_recovery_detail.png"))
```

**Recovery summary:**

- 15 of 16 dates recovered
- 12 at **high confidence** (specific non-FY-end dates, confirmed by V3 API and Excel)
- 3 at **medium confidence** (June 30 fiscal year-end proxies — year likely correct, exact date approximate)
- 1 **not recovered** (P169724)

## 4. Three-scenario comparison

```{r scenario-fig}
#| fig-cap: "Scenario A uses only dates available in the original V2 API. Scenario B adds dates recovered from V3 API and bulk Excel. The only substantive difference in the 1990–2024 window is the addition of P122265 ($200M) in 2014."
knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "fig9_scenario_comparison.png"))
```

```{r scenario-table}
#| echo: false
scen_sum <- tribble(
  ~Scenario, ~Description, ~`Projects (1990–2024)`, ~`Pos. fin. projects`, ~`Total commitments`, ~`% in 2020–2024`, ~`Projects in 2013–2019`, ~`Remaining gap years`,
  "A", "Original V2 API dates only",                  "25", "18", "$3.3B", "71.4%", "0", "2013–2019 all empty",
  "B", "Original + recovered dates (V3/Excel)",       "36", "24", "$3.6B", "64.9%", "3 ($200M in 2014, $0 in 2018×2)", "2013, 2015–2017, 2019",
  "C", "Positive financing only, V2 dates confirmed", "18", "18", "$3.3B", "71.4%", "0", "2013–2019 all empty"
)
scen_sum |>
  kable(caption = "Three-scenario summary (all amounts nominal USD)") |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))
```

```{r enriched-timeline-fig}
#| fig-cap: "Enriched timeline (Scenario B). Amber bars indicate projects whose dates were recovered from the V3 API. The 2014 bar reflects P122265, the $200M Health Networks APL approved July 2014."
knitr::include_graphics(here("figures", "fig1b_portfolio_enriched.png"))
```

**Key differences between Scenario A and B:**

```{r additions-table}
#| echo: false
new_additions |>
  mutate(totalamt_display = if_else(totalamt > 0, fmt_millions(totalamt), "$0")) |>
  arrange(enriched_year) |>
  select(
    `Project ID`  = id,
    `Project name` = project_name,
    `Year (recovered)` = enriched_year,
    `Commitment`  = totalamt_display,
    `Confidence`  = confidence,
    `Status`      = status,
    `Instrument`  = lendinginstr
  ) |>
  kable(caption = "Projects added to Scenario B (had missing dates in Scenario A, recovered dates within 1990–2024)") |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), font_size = 11)
```

## 5. The 2013–2019 gap: assessment

```{r gap-analysis}
#| echo: false
# Build the gap summary table
gap_data <- annual_scen |>
  dplyr::filter(scenario %in% c("A", "B"), year >= 2010, year <= 2024) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = scenario,
                     values_from = c(n, total_usd),
                     names_glue = "{scenario}_{.value}") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    A_total_usd = fmt_millions(A_total_usd),
    B_total_usd = fmt_millions(B_total_usd)
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Year = year,
    `A: Projects` = A_n, `A: Commitments` = A_total_usd,
    `B: Projects` = B_n, `B: Commitments` = B_total_usd
  )

gap_data |>
  kable(caption = "Annual portfolio data 2010–2024 (Scenarios A and B)") |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed")) |>
  row_spec(which(gap_data$Year >= 2013 & gap_data$Year <= 2019) , background = "#fef9ec")
```

### Verdict

The apparent 2013–2019 gap is **both a partial artifact and a real pattern**:

**It is partly a missing-data artifact:**
- P122265 ($200M, Health Networks APL) was approved **2014-07-03** and simply lacked a date in the 
  V2 API. Adding it places a substantial commitment in 2014.
- P163431 ($0) and P167926 ($0) fill 2018 with two genuine project approvals — though neither had 
  positive IBRD financing.

**It is also a real pattern:**
- Even with all recovered dates, **2013, 2015, 2016, 2017, and 2019** still show no confirmed 
  positive IBRD financing commitments.
- P169724 ($100M Learning for All, Dropped) remains unresolved. If it was approved in 2015–2019, 
  it would fill part of the remaining gap. Its document evidence (preparation docs from 2019–2020) 
  suggests it may have been Dropped before the board, meaning no approval date exists.
- The **2015–2019 financing gap appears real**: Costa Rica did not receive substantial new IBRD 
  investment loans during this period. The evidence is consistent with lower Bank engagement during 
  Costa Rica's fiscal deterioration (deficit widening from ~3% to ~8% GDP, 2015–2019).

### Recommendation

The 2013–2019 gap can be presented as follows:

> "World Bank lending to Costa Rica was sparse between 2013 and 2019 by both project count and 
> financing volume. The $200M Health Networks APL (2014) was board-approved during this period but 
> was subsequently dropped; no large investment or policy loans were committed between 2015 and 2019. 
> The pattern is consistent with lower Bank engagement during Costa Rica's pre-reform fiscal stress, 
> though the evidence does not allow a causal claim."

This framing:
- Acknowledges the one meaningful project in 2014 (now visible with recovered dates)
- Accurately reports the 2015–2019 financing absence
- Avoids asserting causation while noting the fiscal context as potentially relevant
- Notes the $100M unresolved project without manufacturing a conclusion

---

## 6. Implications for the analysis

| Impact | Assessment |
|--------|------------|
| Financing totals | Scenario B adds $328M to confirmed in-scope commitments ($3.3B → $3.6B). Six projects with positive financing were missing from the original timeline. |
| 2020–2024 concentration | Drops slightly: 71.4% → 64.9% (still dominant). The shift reflects recovered commitments in 2007, 2010, 2011, and 2014, not new 2020+ projects. |
| The 2013–2019 gap | 2014 now has $200M (P122265). 2018 has two $0 projects. The 2015–2019 financing gap remains. |
| Sector analysis | No change: none of the recovered projects had sector percentages that would affect the sector allocation charts. |
| Text analysis | No change: abstract availability was independent of date recovery. |
| Original figures 1–8 | Still valid for Scenario A. New figures 9, 10, and 1b show the enriched view. |

**Methodology note:** The V2 API (`boardapprovaldate` NULL) and the V3 API / Excel (`boardapprovaldate` populated) are two output channels of the same World Bank database. The discrepancy is a known API version difference, not a data quality issue with the underlying records. The V3/Excel dates are authoritative.
